name: Organize Your Inbox
description: Help the user star important emails, delete junk, archive old messages, or apply a label
prompt:
The user wants to organize their inbox. FIRST ask which one they want to do:
  • **Star** an important email so it stands out
  • **Label** an email (put it in a category folder)
  • **Archive** an email (hide it from the inbox without deleting it)
  • **Delete** an email (move it to Trash)

Reassurance to share before starting: deleted emails go to Trash and stay there for 30 days before disappearing — so a click can be undone. Archived emails are not deleted at all; they just leave the inbox view. Assume Gmail unless they say otherwise.

VISUAL GUIDE — STAR (Gmail): 2 steps.
  Step 1: image_id `gmail-unread-message`. Text: "Find the email in your inbox."
  Step 2: image_id `gmail-star-icon`. Text: "Click the small star ⭐ icon at the left of the email row. It turns yellow. To find all your starred emails later, click **Starred** in the left sidebar."

VISUAL GUIDE — LABEL (Gmail): 3 steps.
  Step 1: image_id `gmail-open-message-view`. Text: "Open the email by clicking it."
  Step 2: image_id `gmail-label-menu`. Text: "At the top, click the **Labels** icon (it looks like a small tag). A menu opens with all your labels."
  Step 3: image_id `gmail-label-menu`. Text: "Click the box next to the label you want, then click **Apply**. The email is now tagged and can be found by clicking that label name in the left sidebar."

VISUAL GUIDE — ARCHIVE (Gmail): 2 steps.
  Step 1: image_id `gmail-open-message-view`. Text: "Open the email by clicking it."
  Step 2: image_id `gmail-archive-button`. Text: "At the top, click the **Archive** icon (a small box with a downward arrow). The email leaves your inbox but is still saved — you can find it again with search."

VISUAL GUIDE — DELETE (Gmail): 2 steps.
  Step 1: image_id `gmail-open-message-view`. Text: "Open the email by clicking it."
  Step 2: image_id `gmail-delete-button`. Text: "At the top, click the **Trash** icon (looks like a small bin). The email moves to Trash and will be gone for good after 30 days. Until then you can still get it back from the Trash folder."
